# Org2

Managed Remote Codex destinations reuse an existing Codex or `~/.ssh/config` host alias and launch `codex app-server --listen stdio://` on that machine over SSH. They require no separately maintained WebSocket tunnel, listener, TLS certificate, or bearer token. The active turn fails visibly if the transport exits, and a later operation starts a fresh remote App Server process rather than replaying work.

> Org2 is a local-first knowledge compiler and runtime for Org-shaped plain text. Ordinary .org2 and .org files are canonical; agendas, graph data, context packets, reports, editor behavior, apps, and websites derive from the shared compiler/runtime.

Installed agents should begin with:

    org2 agent capabilities
    org2 --help
    org2 agent --help

The first command emits the machine-readable `org2:capabilities:v1` manifest. Mutating commands generally preview unless `--apply` is provided. Preserve citations, IDs, provenance, and review state; place generated work in `views/` or `compiled/` before promotion into canonical notes.

Publishing includes disclosure-safe single-document destinations, ordinary single-file HTML, multi-file HTML projects, and Beamer-compatible presentations. `org2 publish document --file REPORT.org2 --to web --out-dir DIR` previews a sealed web bundle; `--line N` selects one subtree. The same safe projection can be rendered as an embedded-image DOCX and converted into a new or guarded existing Google Doc with `--to google-docs`. It strips private Org metadata, internal links, comments, raw HTML, and runtime data before either destination receives content. A static bundle does not enforce authentication; the selected host owns public, secret-link, or per-person access, while Google Drive owns Google Doc permissions. Use `org2 export beamer --file TALK.org2` to preview TeX generation, add `--apply` to write it, and add `--pdf` to compile through `pdflatex` (or the command selected by `--latex-engine`). Presentation structure is compiled from the shared Org2 AST; legacy `BEAMER_*` properties and backend-neutral `SLIDE_*` properties map into the same presentation model.

Explicit color presentation uses preserved custom links rather than inferred column names: `[[color:red][urgent]]` binds foreground, `[[color:bg=yellow][review]]` binds background, and `[[color:fg=white;bg=#b42318][blocked]]` binds both. These non-navigating spans work in ordinary inline content and AI chat; a sole binding in a table cell applies to the whole cell. Invalid or arbitrary CSS remains an ordinary link.

Org pipe tables can carry structured `#+TBLFM:` spreadsheet formulas. `org2 table recalculate --file FILE` previews safe deterministic evaluation and `--apply` writes changed cells atomically. The shared renderer, Mac app, CLI, LSP, VS Code, Vim, and Tree-sitter surfaces recognize the same formula lines. Arithmetic, relative/absolute references, ranges, vector aggregates, numeric formats, and duration modes are supported; Emacs Lisp, remote tables, and arbitrary Calc extensions remain lossless but are never executed.

The native OpenOrg for macOS consumes that shared presentation classification to select document or slide preview automatically per file, while retaining an explicit per-file override. Its compiled-PDF view supports slide-number navigation, previous/next and first/last keyboard movement, and fit-relative zoom without recompiling the deck.

Every loaded Org node in the native OpenOrg for macOS shows an editable entity-type badge. Common and custom choices are persisted as an `ORG2_ENTITY_TYPE` property on the file or heading. Full-page people, companies, and projects include a bounded action-item panel backed by `org2 query actions`. The deterministic query combines TODOs directly linked or related through entity properties with TODOs inherited from containing meetings that link to the entity, plus dated recent completions. It uses the incremental corpus cache and does not invoke an agent or generate a node brief.

Portable corpus identity lives in the root `org2.json`. Use `org2 corpus show|validate|init` before mounting a corpus for team or agent use. `org2 workspace agenda|search` can combine read-only results from repeatable, explicitly named `--mount` paths and attaches corpus identity to every result. Writes remain scoped to the active corpus; an agent must not inherit all human-visible mounts by convenience.

Portable external-source intent may also live in `org2.json`, but credentials and machine paths must not. Use `org2 source list|doctor|status|bind|schedule|import|sync` to orchestrate the external `slacrawl` and `notcrawl` binaries. `source import` previews bounded raw captures and review-required Org2 packets; `source sync PROFILE --ingest --apply` refreshes and stages them. A profile may declare a validated interval or daily schedule; `source schedule` previews or atomically applies cadence changes and pause/resume state. The Mac app exposes Run Now and per-connector schedule controls, executes due schedules while running, catches up after wake or launch, and keeps last-attempt/next-run/error state local to that machine. Bindings live outside the corpus under the machine's Org2 index home, and the Mac app can keep a Notion token in Keychain, so clients can invoke the same corpus profile with independent local authorization.

The native OpenOrg for macOS also exposes a discoverable chat slash-command layer. Its local commands reuse shared search, backlink, lint, render, and publish semantics; agent-assisted `/brief` and `/summarize` receive selected source context with citations. User-invocable skills in the active corpus's `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` are loaded into autocomplete locally, labeled as skills, and forwarded to either the OpenClaw or Codex runtime without requiring Gateway discovery. When the live OpenClaw Gateway supports `commands.list`, its runtime-native, skill, and plugin commands for the selected agent are also merged into autocomplete and forwarded unchanged through `chat.send`; they do not use HTTP compatibility. Gateway progress intentionally exposed by the provider is stored with the assistant reply, while repetitive tool completion events are grouped into a compact work log. See OpenOrg reference for details.

The Mac Files surface and quick open include CSV files. Opening a local CSV link from rendered Org2 content or AI chat keeps it inside the detail pane, where table and raw-text modes share the app's ordinary autosave, Command-S, stale-write protection, and file undo behavior. CSV data remains an ordinary file and is excluded from Org semantic indexing.

The Mac app can optionally pair as a narrow local-edit node as well as an operator UI. With this setting enabled and connected, chat turns use typed `org2.workspace.read`, `org2.workspace.patch.preview`, and `org2.workspace.patch.apply` node commands instead of Gateway filesystem writes. Reads include the effective selected editor draft; previews are bound to SHA-256 inputs; apply rechecks them, stays inside the corpus where the turn began, and supplies the exact per-turn change summary. The node exposes no generic shell. This requires the `org2-lifecycle` plugin's node policy, node-role pairing, and the selected agent's `nodes` tool.

New Mac AI-chat threads expose an OpenClaw/Codex runtime picker beside the composer controls. The runtime can change while the thread is empty and locks after its first message. Adjacent model and reasoning pickers load the runtime-supported catalog and persist optional per-thread overrides; selecting Default clears the override. The native app Settings window can add persistent user-authored AI chat instructions, choose current-corpus or all-loaded-corpora read access, and select Read Only, Workspace Write, or opt-in Full Access for local Codex turns. Workspace Write is the default. Codex-owned `.codex` state remains protected in that mode, so workflows that acquire leases under `~/.codex` require Full Access; enable it only for trusted threads. The authorized local/configured remote roots are captured per turn; secondary corpora are read-only, while preview/apply stays locked to the active corpus. OpenClaw applies explicit overrides through the live Gateway session, while Codex passes them to `codex app-server` turns. In-flight turns retain the context, transcript, authorized read roots, and local-edit write root of their originating corpus while the visible workspace switches away or back. For Codex, Org2 launches a long-lived `codex app-server`, delegates ChatGPT subscription authentication to Codex, and stores only the external Codex thread ID with the local transcript. Client-side `org2_workspace_read`, `org2_workspace_patch_preview`, and `org2_workspace_patch_apply` tools continue to enforce the same turn-origin corpus guard, unsaved-editor-aware reads, SHA-bound preview/apply transaction, and exact per-turn change summary as the OpenClaw node. API-key-authenticated Codex is not accepted on this subscription path. Codex threads bypass the OpenClaw Gateway and lifecycle plugin.

Normal Mac Workspace chat turns include a non-secret snapshot of the active corpus's configured Org2 source profiles and general source-discovery guidance. OpenClaw uses `org2 source list/status` and the returned profile IDs, types, scopes, raw zones, and review zones as the authority, searches staged source material as ordinary Org2 text, and refreshes a matching enabled profile when fresher material is needed. It asks the user about setup only when `org2 source doctor` reports a specific missing machine-local binding or credential.

OpenClaw is currently the deepest native adapter. The repository's `integrations/openclaw` lifecycle plugin records substantial main-agent turns, subagent executions, and cron executions as correlated durable runs. Scheduled workflow executions share a stable logical-work ID but receive distinct numbered attempt records; declared event/fresh-path gates create a safe skipped attempt instead of starting expensive workflow steps when no new signal exists. The plugin preserves available provider/model and usage metadata, records terminal outcome summaries, leaves approval or clarification boundaries open, continues an approved workflow in its correlated chat session, and verifies the Mac app's selected portable corpus identity against its single configured write corpus. Other agents can use the same run/workflow files, cited retrieval, CLI JSON, and MCP surfaces.

Goals and named workers are portable corpus concepts. `org2 goal` manages `org2:goal:v1` records under `goals/`; `org2 agent-profile` manages `org2:agent-profile:v1` records under `agent-profiles/`. OpenClaw and Codex are runtimes, not agent profile IDs. Profiles may bind a non-secret runtime identity such as `openclaw:customer-support` or `codex:default`; resolve one with `org2 agent-profile resolve --runtime RUNTIME --runtime-agent-id ID --dir CORPUS --json`. Preserve returned `agentRef` and `goalRef` on `run create`, `workflow run`, or delegated TODO properties. Existing selected-work refs take precedence, `ASSIGNEE` remains only a readable label, and unbound identities must remain unset rather than guessed.

Durable delegation uses generated run records under `.org2/runs/` and authored workflow files under the visible `workflows/` directory. Org2 continues to read the legacy `.org2/workflows/` location. Discover the interfaces with:

    org2 run --help
    org2 workflow --help
    org2 doctor --dir CORPUS --json
    org2 ledger list account-outreach --eligible --dir CORPUS --json
    org2 ledger resolve account-outreach --identity NAME_OR_EMAIL_OR_DOMAIN --dir CORPUS --json
    org2 approvals --dir CORPUS --recursive --format json
    org2 review list --dir CORPUS --json
    org2 mcp serve --dir CORPUS

AI chat automation is also corpus-owned rather than private Mac UI state. `org2 thread list/show` reads `.org2/openclaw-chat.json`; `thread settle/reopen`, `thread configure --auto-settle never|SECONDS`, and `thread auto-settle` preview by default and require `--apply` to write. `thread post THREAD_ID --message TEXT --author NAME --agent-ref AGENT_REF --source REF --idempotency-key KEY` previews an agent-attributed, no-turn background message; `--apply` queues an append-only envelope under `.org2/ai-chat-inbox/`. The Mac app drains queued posts while running or when the corpus opens, persists them into the named thread, reopens a settled destination, marks it unread, and follows the normal notification path without invoking or steering an AI runtime. Settled threads retain messages, session keys, context, and searchability. Auto-settlement excludes the selected thread plus pinned, unread, or pending threads and threads whose latest delivery is still sending, failed, or interrupted. Empty threads and recovered historical failures remain eligible.

Runs preserve goals, acceptance criteria, cited inputs, plans, risk, provider metadata, budgets, artifacts, approvals, validation, comments, and observable events. Workflow packages declare inputs, capabilities, writes, outputs, triggers, checks, approval boundaries, and compatibility. External MCP/connector data that becomes durable work should be stored as a provenance-bearing snapshot; credentials stay outside the corpus.
Run and workflow writes are guarded and atomic. `org2 run show RUN_ID --with-revision --json` returns the current SHA-256 file revision; pass it back as `--if-revision REVISION` when state crosses a client/request boundary. The CLI and MCP refuse stale revisions, concurrent locks, duplicate creates, and readable run fields that disagree with canonical machine state instead of silently replacing newer source.
Recurring account workflows must resolve all available stable identities before creating work. Do not proceed through ambiguity or source drift by guessing.
`org2 doctor --dir CORPUS --json` is the read-only integrity check for this boundary. It reports contradictory run/approval state, duplicate provider decision keys, conflicting or overlapping recurring attempts, unmanaged OpenClaw cron series, broken projected links, readable-header drift from canonical run state, and likely duplicate open headings. Errors return a nonzero exit code. The doctor never repairs source automatically; inspect its cited evidence and use canonical lifecycle operations or an explicit reviewed source edit.
For account-oriented recurring work, use `org2 ledger` instead of appending global bookkeeping to one agent file. Curated account records live at `notes/LEDGER/accounts/ACCOUNT_ID.org2`; raw exports and provider payloads remain under `raw/`, and generated selections belong in `views/`. Creates, updates, and events preview unless `--apply` is present. Stable identity keys and ledger-wide event idempotency keys prevent duplicate accounts and repeated actions. Link native run approvals by `runId/approvalId`; do not copy their decision status into the ledger. `outreach-sent` requires an external receipt ID and, when approval-linked, an approved canonical decision. Eligibility remains closed after proposal/approval until a sent, canceled, or skipped event settles that outreach cycle. Readable event history and structured event state must agree: `org2 doctor` reports out-of-band drift and later structured writes fail closed instead of erasing it.
`org2 approvals` is the unified pending-decision queue. A `kind=run` item names the exact `runId` and `approvalId` in `.org2/runs/`, carries the immutable SHA-256 fingerprint of its review material, exposes deterministic provider `decisionKeys` when available, includes the run goal/status and remaining approval count, and must be decided through `org2 run approval-decide --fingerprint FINGERPRINT`. Approval decisions are item-scoped: rejecting or canceling one action leaves sibling approvals pending, and a fully decided boundary resumes with rejected or canceled actions excluded. Recording one approval as completed elsewhere cancels only that approval with an external receipt; it never completes the containing run. `--decision revised` keeps the workflow open for replacement material and requires `--note "Requested changes"` so that work has durable direction. A `kind=headline` item remains an ordinary cited corpus heading unless its `ORG2_RUN_ID` resolves unambiguously to a run approval, in which case it is a derived projection and is omitted as a second writable decision. Preserve the exact `Provider draft: PROVIDER:TOOL:DRAFT_ID` line and request replacements on the existing run. The CLI reuses matching pending material, supersedes older versions without falsely approving them, rejects stale decisions, and closes dedicated duplicate review runs after the canonical decision. Execution guards resolve both pending and decided authority with `org2 run approval-resolve --decision-key KEY --json`; private adapter mappings never override that result. Do not create a second heading or run to mirror a run approval.
Agents must use `org2 run block RUN_ID --reason "Specific clarification or next action"`; reasonless blocked runs are rejected because they give the reviewer nothing actionable to answer. If the run has a pending approval, leave it in `waiting-approval`. Only an independent clarification or operational blocker may add `--separate-from-approval`, and approval-shaped reasons are rejected even with that override.
Agents must complete durable runs with `org2 run complete RUN_ID --summary "What happened"`; use repeatable `--highlight` and `--next-action` flags when useful. The summary is the primary human-facing result, not a log line or a restatement of the goal.
Agents must not complete runs whose artifacts remain `review-required`. After a human decision, use `org2 run artifact-review RUN_ID ARTIFACT_ID --status reviewed|rejected --actor NAME`; for linked Org/Org2 files inside the corpus, the command updates both the run snapshot and artifact metadata.
Only after a person confirms that an unfinished run's outcome was completed outside the workflow, use `org2 run complete-external RUN_ID --summary "Where or how it was completed" --actor NAME`. This explicit resolution marks unfinished workflow steps skipped and preserves pending approvals, unreviewed artifacts, and warning metadata as historical evidence; agents must not infer external completion on their own.
Use `org2 run reopen-external RUN_ID --summary "Corrected open-run outcome" --actor NAME` only to repair a run mistakenly completed externally from `waiting-approval`; it restores the same run and retained approval identities to the pending queue.
Agents and runtime adapters should record observable execution metadata with `org2 run runtime RUN_ID --provider ID --model ID` plus available `--tokens-used`, `--cost-used-usd`, or `--elapsed-seconds` values. Credentials never belong in the run.
